doc.title: Burrill Crohn interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, January 3, 2012

title: Inspiration as pregnancy; films as children
summary: He says finishing the Sangeeta film is certain, and compares inspiration to conception and his films to children.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: film about this guy. So here I am. I don’t know how I’m doing it and whether I can raise enough money to finish it — I will.
But you got the inspiration which is step one, right?

That’s right. And sometimes — we’re going to get far out here — inspiration is like getting pregnant. It’s like something, some idea comes and impregnates you. And then you’ve given birth to this thing and you have to nurture this thing into being, into adulthood, which is the finished film. I don’t have children of my own, as far as I know, and someone has said, “Yeah but you have your films” which is your children. Each one of them came to me as an idea and I nurtured them into being and let them loose into the world. And they’ll be there long after I’m gone, for better or for worse.
